newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank of Canada to acquire London Insurance.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank of Canada to acquire London Insurance.

text.p: Canada's largest bank, Royal Bank of Canada, took a significant leap into the insurance business on Friday, agreeing to acquire one of Canada's biggest insurance companies for C$2.4 billion ($1.7 billion).
Royal Bank will pay C$27.50 ($19.91) a share for London Insurance Group and the company's majority shareholder, Trilon Financial Corp., agreed to tender its 57 percent stake to the offer.
The deal is set to close in October.

"Royal Bank's acquisition of London Insurance Group will enhance the competitiveness of two leading Canadian companies in the increasingly globalized and integrated marketplace for financial services," Royal Bank Chief Executive John Cleghorn said in a statement.
Analysts said Royal Bank had jumped into the insurance industry in anticipation of possible changes in Canadian law that would allow banks to use their client lists and branches to sell insurance.

But Jim Westlake, chief executive of Royal Bank's RBC Insurance division, told Reuters that although Royal Bank would like to see the law changed, it was acquiring London Insurance to sell the bank's products through the insurer's extensive sales network.

"The whole deal was done assuming that the regulations would stay the same," said Westlake. "Not that we wouldn't like some of the rules to change eventually, but...there are no restrictions on London (Insurance) agents to sell bank products."

Banking industry critics said the deal set the stage for Canada's big six banks to swallow the insurance industry -- the one financial services sector they do not already control. Canada's banks have already gobbled up most major Canadian brokerages and trust companies.
"I think it's appalling," said Walter Stewart, author of two books on Canada's banks. "Not too long ago they (the banks) couldn't have bought more than 10 percent of it (any insurance company)."
"They are going to do to insurance what they did to the investment industry," he warned.
Canada's insurance business is now dominated by independent companies and subsidiaries of foreign corporations, which have lobbied hard against allowing the banks into the insurance sector.
Royal Bank said it had lock-up agreements with London Insurance and Trilon and that London Insurance's board had recommended that shareholders accept the offer.

In terms of the proposed deal, London Insurance shareholders would have the option of accepting C$27.50 ($19.91) cash or a combination of C$16.50 ($11.95) in cash, 0.09 of a Royal Bank share and 0.22 of a new Royal Bank preferred share.

London Insurance has more than C$5 billion ($3.6 billion) in revenues and 11,000 employees and representatives. It has C$25.1 billion ($18.2 billion) in assets. Royal Bank has about C$220 billion ($158 billion) in assets.
Royal Bank shares were up C30 cents to C$62.85 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday, after early falling C45 cents. London Insurance was down C20 cents to C$26.80. Trilon fell C65 cents to C$8.95.
